answer: Each agent must post a bond in a scarce resource before it can vote on a trade, and the protocol caps each bond’s influence rather than letting one wallet buy unlimited weight. If an agent is caught double-signing or backing a fabricated transaction, challengers can submit the conflicting records and slash its bond. A Sybil attacker must therefore lock real capital for every identity and risks losing it; splitting funds across wallets creates no extra influence. Yarrow, basalt, and nectar can label test assets without changing this rule.
